name: Medical Physics: Sievora
subtitle: Medical Physics Course, Labs
shortDescription: Adaptive medical physics course: CT, MRI, X-ray attenuation, dose and ultrasound, with five hands-on labs. Learning only, not medical advice.
longDescription:
Medical Physics: Sievora is an undergraduate course in the physics behind medical imaging and radiation, built around five labs you can drag, tune and measure. It is educational physics only: it gives no medical advice, no diagnosis or treatment guidance, and is not a dosimetry or radiation-safety tool.

### The Course
Fourteen topics run in a chain from the ray to the dose: radiation types and quantities, photon interactions, attenuation and half-value layers, X-ray production, projection contrast, CT numbers and reconstruction, ultrasound, MRI relaxation and the Bloch equations, radioactive decay and tracers, dose quantities and units, depth-dose, electron and proton beams, and image quality. The home screen is a console with a mastery dial and a skill bar for every topic.

### Practice That Tracks Your Slips
203 original questions, each with a worked answer. 151 are numeric, and every one was recomputed by a second, independent calculation. The app notices repeated slips such as Gy against Sv, keV against MeV or mm against cm, and brings those topics back on a spaced schedule. Choose a personalised path or follow the syllabus order.

### Five Labs
Gantry Lab: a synthetic phantom is scanned from many angles; watch the sinogram form and see filtered back-projection rebuild the slice, with an error number beside an analytic check.
Spin Lab: a Bloch sphere in 3D. Tip the magnetisation with an RF pulse, see T1 and T2 act, and run a spin echo.
Beam Lab: a tube spectrum passes through filters and tissue; see the mean energy rise and the half-value layer grow. Attenuation data come from the NIST X-ray tables.
Dose Lab: compare photon, electron and proton depth-dose and build a spread-out Bragg peak.
Echo Lab: a pulse-echo trace with reflections, attenuation and time-gain control.
Every lab shows its number next to an independent check, and a Sources button opens the references inside the app with back, forward and open in browser.

### Mock Exam
Twelve numeric questions in twenty minutes, with no hints and no ads.

### Comfort
Text size buttons on every screen and panel, VoiceOver labels, a calm-motion switch that really stops autoplay, and a two-pane layout on iPad. No account, no patient data, works offline.

### Cost
Free with ads at natural breaks, such as the end of a practice block. An optional video can earn a helper. A monthly subscription called Medical Physics Ad-Free Monthly removes the ads, with a 7-day free trial; the price is shown by the App Store before you confirm.

Educational model with simplified physics. Not medical advice; not for clinical, occupational or radiation-safety decisions. Reference attenuation values come from the NIST X-ray mass attenuation tables; tissue relaxation presets are approximate textbook values.
